decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display has its own page and fits the firm's announced display-solutions direction, and since 2020-2021 offer no contrary evidence, management would hold to its earlier commitment.
The pegboard-back display is a visible part of the display range the firm has invested in, and any weak demand can be blamed on temporary pandemic-era retail disruption.
The standard quarter-pallet display is core to the firm's display portfolio, so a firm committed to this line would continue it.
The eighth-pallet display completes the publicly presented pallet-size range, and management would persist with it to justify the 2018 range launch.
The wooden pallet is less central to a paper-products firm, but it was launched and presented alongside the cardboard range, so commitment and sunk costs favor keeping it for now.
The media display serves a shrinking niche, but management can attribute weak results to temporary market conditions and would stand by its earlier decision.
